newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Renault workers vote against long strike.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Renault workers vote against long strike.

text.p: Workers of the Renault plant in Vilvoorde, Belgium, have voted against an all-out strike against plans to close their factory.
"A majority has voted to resume work and hold regular 24-hour strikes," union leader Karel Gacoms told BRTN radio on Tuesday, following the vote late on Monday.
Seventy-five percent of 2,258 workers voted against an all-out strike and in favour of regular one-day strikes.
An even larger majority, 87 percent, voted in favour of negotiations with management about a social package for workers when the plant is closed.
But Gacoms added that he feared that work could still be interrupted by a minority of workers.

"One group (of workers) has problems accepting the vote, I hope they will accept what the majority has decided," he said. The assembly line could easily be blocked if a small group refused to cooperate.
Renault has decided to close its Vilvoorde plant on July 31. The news of the closure on February 27 sparked a wave of protest actions in Belgium and abroad.

Before the French parliamentary election on Sunday, the French Socialist Party had said it would push for a review of the decision to close the plant if it won. The second round of the elections is on June 1, following successes by the socialists in the first round.
The French government has a 46 percent stake in Renault.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
